phase_name: Felt-Quality Build — Axis 3: Command Palette + Keyboard Control
objective: Build axis 3 — 'every action reachable by button, shortcut, or palette search' — the lone unbuilt north-star control/joy axis, making the GUI keyboard-competitive with the terminal it's meant to replace.
recommendation: Build axis 3 as a custom command registry + Cmd+K palette + keyboard shortcuts over EXISTING actions (Option A) — it's the last north-star axis and the only thing making the GUI keyboard-competitive with the terminal (zero shortcuts exist today). But A1 is real: the spec gates ported features on a 'used weekly' dogfood test (spec:80) that has never run because the live drive was deferred 4x. If you want axis 3 shipped proven-by-use, Option B pairs the build with finally running that live drive at delivery.

options.label: A — Custom palette + keyboard, palette-only (Recommended)
options.description: Hand-rolled command registry + Cmd+K palette + keyboard shortcuts over existing actions (stop / approve / deny / revert / focus) + the one genuinely-missing action (new conversation). No new dep, no security items. Mechanics-tested; felt ships on your judgment.
options.reasoning: Axis 3 is the last unbuilt north-star axis and the only thing making the GUI keyboard-competitive with the terminal it's meant to replace — zero keyboard shortcuts exist today and the gate/revert are mouse-only. The Ph109 'owned not adopted' ethos favors custom; ~6 static commands don't justify a runtime dep in a strict-CSP, freshly-sandbox-hardened app. The pure command registry outlives whatever the palette UI becomes.
options.consequences: Commits to building axis 3 BEFORE its spec 'used weekly' precondition is demonstrated — the bet is that supply makes the loop reach-for-able. Defers the live window-drive a 5th time. Vercel-output redaction + cross-platform sandbox stay OUT (a future security phase, since you chose to pivot away from security this round).

options.label: B — Palette + finally run the live drive at delivery
options.description: Same build as A, but this phase's acceptance bar is you actually driving the app — closing the 4x-deferred live window-drive and the spec's 'used weekly' precondition. Axis 3 ships proven-by-use, and the drive populates the real UX quick-win list for Ph114.
options.reasoning: Directly retires the A1 risk: instead of betting supply creates demand, you confirm the loop is reach-for-able by using it. It's the LAST axis — a natural moment to close the standing live-drive debt and ground the next phase in observed friction rather than guesses.
options.consequences: Adds a maintainer-time delivery step (the drive) you've deferred every phase since 109. If the drive surfaces big friction, Ph113 acceptance may spill into follow-on fixes. Trades a fast ship for a grounded one.

options.label: C — Adopt cmdk instead of hand-rolling
options.description: Use the cmdk library for the palette (battle-tested fuzzy-search + keyboard nav + a11y) instead of a custom component; same command set + shortcuts.
options.reasoning: Faster path to a polished palette with good fuzzy-matching and accessibility out of the box; less custom UI code to own and maintain.
options.consequences: Adds a runtime dependency + its supply-chain surface to an app whose last phases were literally about sandboxing untrusted code; cuts against the Ph109 'owned not adopted' ethos. Marginal benefit for ~6 static commands.

assumptions.text: Building axis 3 now will make the loop reach-for-able (supply creates demand) — even though the spec gates ported features on a 'used weekly' dogfood test (spec:80) that has never run, because the live drive was deferred 4x. If FALSE: a correctly-built axis the maintainer doesn't actually reach for — effort an honest dogfood would have deprioritized.

Every target action (gate approve/deny, revert, stop, new-conversation) is dispatchable from a new App-mounted palette through EXISTING bridge channels, needing no new privileged host path. If FALSE: the palette would need a channel that touches the gate/security core — breaking the no-new-privileged-path invariant the GUI phases have held since Ph108.

There is no unstated felt-quality friction you'd want bundled here — the 'UX quick-wins' from the objective are genuinely closed (icon/typed-diff/flaky-e2e all done) or are security/separate-phase work. If FALSE: a real felt win gets dropped by scoping the phase palette-only.

Mechanics-only tests + felt-on-your-judgment, with the live window-drive still deferred, is an acceptable exit bar for this axis (Ph109-112 precedent). If FALSE: you want the drive run as part of THIS phase's acceptance — which is Option B.

open_decisions: Run the 4x-deferred live drive now as the acceptance bar (Option B)?
